goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code at line 22, the code executes: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The variable `h` comes from splitting the embeddable_hosts setting value by newlines. This value is user-controlled data from site settings that is directly interpolated into a SQL query without any sanitization or escaping. This is a classic SQL injection vulnerability. An attacker who could set the embeddable_hosts setting to a malicious value could inject arbitrary SQL. This is a real security issue.

The method appears to work correctly - it parses the URI, extracts the host, and does a case-insensitive lookup. Without a specific description of what the problem is, I cannot verify if there's a real issue. The finding is incomplete/vague.

The finding references lines 10 and 15 in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb but doesn't specify what the actual problem is. Looking at the code, line 10 is `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` in the update method, and line 15 is `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` in the destroy method. Both methods don't check if `host` is nil before calling methods on it (save_host(host) and host.destroy respectively). If the host is not found, this would cause a NoMethodError. However, the finding description is incomplete - it just references file and line numbers without stating what the problem is. Without a clear description of the issue, I cannot verify this is a real finding, though there does appear to be a potential nil check issue.
